ideas.title: Presentation Pacer
ideas.summary: A browser-based slide practice tool that tracks per-slide timing and uses Claude to give immediate, actionable coaching on pacing and clarity — no video recording or backend required.
ideas.description: A browser-based presentation practice tool where you paste your slide content or upload a deck, then advance slides with the space bar while speaking. On finish, the Claude API analyzes your per-slide timing and an optional Web Speech API transcript to give coaching: which slides you rushed, where your explanation was unclear, and concrete pacing suggestions. Everything runs client-side with no backend required.
keyFeatures: Paste or upload slide content; advance slides with keyboard
Per-slide timer tracking with visual heatmap of fast vs. slow slides
Optional live speech transcription via Web Speech API
Claude API post-session coaching report with specific, actionable feedback
Export coaching report as markdown or PDF
ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind, Web Speech API, Claude API (client-side via SDK), optional PDF export with jsPDF
ideas.whyInteresting: Public speaking is a genuine pain point for students and developers alike, yet most practice tools are either expensive or require video recording and manual review. This makes AI coaching frictionless and immediate.
ideas.inspiredBy: HN discussion on developer productivity tools (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46345827) and the growing trend of AI coaching tools for async skill-building

ideas.title: AI Research Methods Lab
ideas.summary: Students design hypothesis-driven experiments about LLM behavior, run them automatically, and write structured mini-reports — teaching scientific method alongside AI evaluation literacy.
ideas.description: A classroom tool where students design and run small-scale AI behavior experiments. A student writes a hypothesis, defines test cases and a scoring rubric, and the tool automatically runs the experiment across multiple Claude API calls, logs results in a structured table, and walks the student through writing a mini research report with methods, results, and discussion sections.
keyFeatures: Hypothesis and variable definition form with guided prompts
Automated experiment runner that sends batched API calls and logs structured results
Side-by-side response diff viewer for comparing conditions
AI-assisted write-up scaffold (methods, results, discussion templates)
Class dashboard for instructors to see all student experiments and share interesting findings
ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind (frontend), Flask + Supabase (backend and result storage), Claude API for experiment execution and write-up coaching
ideas.whyInteresting: Most AI literacy curricula focus on using AI tools, not on evaluating them rigorously. This gives students a taste of real empirical AI research methodology without requiring ML expertise or GPU access.
ideas.inspiredBy: Karpathy's autoresearch project (https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch), which showed the value of having AI agents run systematic ML experiments autonomously

ideas.title: Synthetic Learner Studio
ideas.summary: Students build a multi-agent system where AI agents role-play diverse student archetypes, then iterate their lesson explanation until all synthetic learners are satisfied — teaching both empathy and agent design.
ideas.description: Students build a multi-agent system in which each AI agent plays a 'synthetic student' with a distinct, persistent learning profile: a visual learner, an anxious test-taker, a fast grasper, and a misconception-holder. The real student feeds these synthetic learners a lesson explanation and observes how each responds differently, then iterates their teaching until all profiles are satisfied. The exercise builds empathy for diverse learners while teaching practical AI agent design.
keyFeatures: Configurable synthetic student profiles with persistent memory across a conversation session
Side-by-side chat UI showing all learner agents responding in parallel
Satisfaction meter per profile that updates as the lesson improves
Profile editor so instructors can add domain-specific misconceptions for a course
Session export showing which explanations resonated with which profiles and why
ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind (frontend), Flask + Supabase (session storage and profile management), Claude API for each synthetic student agent with distinct system prompts and persistent context
ideas.whyInteresting: Building a multi-agent empathy tool forces students to think deeply about diverse learning needs while practicing real agent orchestration — two difficult skills that rarely appear in the same assignment.
ideas.inspiredBy: Inworld AI's NPC character work applied to pedagogy, and AI-in-education trends around understanding diverse learning styles (https://www.analyticsinsight.net/artificial-intelligence/top-10-ai-game-development-tools-in-2026-you-should-know)
